\label{prop:std_form_matrix_ampl}

If $(M,H,J,P)$ is a standard form and $P^{(n)}=\{\sum_{j,k=1}^n \xi_{jk}\otimes E_{jk}\in H\otimes S^2_n\mid \sum_{j,k=1}^n x_j J x_k J\xi_{j,k}\in P\}$, then $(M\otimes M_n(\mathbb C),H\otimes S^2_n,J\otimes J_n,P^{(n)})$ is a standard form.

label: prop:KMS_state_inv
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:KMS_state_inv}
    Let $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on $M$. If $\varphi$, $\psi$ are faithful normal states on $M$ that are invariant under $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ and $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is KMS-symmetric with respect to $\varphi$, then it is also KMS-symmetric with respect to $\psi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $N=\{x\in M\mid \Phi_t(x)=x\text{ for all }t\geq 0\}$. By \cite[Theorem A]{Wat79}, the set $N$ is a von Neumann subalgebra of $M$, for every $x\in M$ the limit $E(x)=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac 1t\int_0^t \Phi_s(x)\,ds$ exists in the strong operator topology and $E$ is a faithful normal conditional expectation such that $\varphi\circ E=\varphi$ and $\psi\circ E=\psi$. In particular, $N$ is invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$ and $\sigma^\psi$ by Takesaki's theorem \cite[Theorem IX.4.2]{Tak03}.

    Let $H_N=\overline{N\Omega_\varphi}\subset L^2(M)$. Since $N$ is invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$, the subspace $H_N$ is invariant under $\Delta_\varphi^{it}$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$. Thus, if $x\in N$, then $J(x\Omega_\varphi)=\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}(x^\ast \Omega_\varphi)\in H_N$. By continuity, it follows that $J(H_N)\subset H_N$. Let $J_N=J|_{H_N}$ and $P_N=\overline{\{x J_N x J_N \Omega_\varphi\mid x\in N\}}$. 
    
    By \cite[Remark 1.2]{Haa75}, the quadruple $(N,H_N,J_N,P_N)$ is a standard form. Therefore, there exists a unique $\xi\in P_N$ such that $\psi(x)=\langle \xi,x\xi\rangle$ for all $x\in N$ by \cite[Lemma 2.10]{Haa75}. Let $h_n\in N$ such that $h_n\Omega_\varphi\to \xi$. For $y\in M$ we have
    \begin{align*}
        \langle \xi,y\xi\rangle=\lim_{n\to \infty}\varphi(h_n^\ast yh_n)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\varphi(h_n^\ast E(y)h_n)=\langle \xi,E(y)\xi\rangle=\psi(E(y))=\psi(y).
    \end{align*}
    Since $P_N\subset L^2_+(M)$, we conclude that $\xi=\Omega_\psi$. Now we get 
    \begin{align*}
        \langle \Phi_t(x)\Omega_\psi,\Delta_\psi^{1/2}y \Omega_\psi\rangle&
        =\langle J y\Omega_\psi,\Phi_t(x)^\ast\Omega_\psi\rangle\\
        &=\lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \Phi_t(x)J y J h_n \Omega_\varphi,h_n\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle \Phi_t(h_n^\ast x h_n)Jy J\Omega_\varphi,\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle\Phi_t(h_n^\ast x h_n)\Omega_\varphi,\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}y\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle h_n^\ast xh_n\Omega_\varphi,\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}\Phi_t(y)\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\langle x\Omega_\psi,\Delta_\psi^{1/2}\Phi_t(y)\Omega_\psi\rangle
    \end{align*}
    for all $x,y\in M$.

label: lem:Moreau_reg_Dir
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Moreau_reg_Dir}
    If $\mathcal E$ is a quantum Dirichlet form on $L^2(M)$ and $\varepsilon>0$, then the Moreau regularization $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$ is also a quantum Dirichlet form.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $0\leq\mathcal E_\varepsilon\leq \mathcal E$, the property $\mathcal E_\varepsilon(\Omega_\varphi)=0$ is immediate. If $\xi\in L^2(M)$, then
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal E_\varepsilon(J\xi)
        &=\inf_{\eta\in L^2(M)}\mathcal E(\eta)+\frac 1 \varepsilon\lVertJ \xi-\eta\rVert^2\\
        &=\inf_{\eta\in L^2(M)}\mathcal E(J \eta)+\frac 1 \varepsilon\lVertJ(\xi-\eta)\rVert^2\\
        &=\mathcal E_\varepsilon(\xi).
    \end{align*}
    Moreover, if $\xi\in L^2(M)^{J}$, then
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal E_\varepsilon(\xi_+)&=\inf_{\eta\in L^2(M) }\mathcal E(\eta)+\frac 1 \varepsilon\lVert\xi_+-\eta\rVert^2\\
        &\leq \inf_{\eta\in L^2(M)}\mathcal E(\eta_+)+\frac 1 \varepsilon\lVert\xi_+-\eta_+\rVert^2\\
        &\leq \inf_{\eta\in L^2(M)}\mathcal E(\eta)+\frac 1 \varepsilon \lVert\xi-\eta\rVert^2\\
        &=\mathcal E(\xi),
    \end{align*}
    where we used that $\xi\mapsto \xi_+$ is $1$-Lipschitz in the second inequality. Thus $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$ is a conservative Dirichlet form.

    Finally, since
    \begin{align*}
        (\mathcal E^{(n)})_\varepsilon((\xi_{jk})_{j,k})&=\inf_{\eta\in L^2(M)}\sum_{j,k=1}^n\mathcal E(\eta_{jk})+\frac 1 \varepsilon \sum_{j,k=1}^n\lVert\xi_{jk}-\eta_{jk}\rVert^2\\
        &=\sum_{j,k=1}^n\inf_{\eta\in L^2(M)} \mathcal E(\eta)+\frac 1 \varepsilon \lVert\xi_{jk}-\eta\rVert^2\\
        &=\sum_{j,k=1}^n \mathcal E_\varepsilon(\xi_{jk})\\
        &=(\mathcal E_\varepsilon)^{(n)}((\xi_{jk})_{j,k}),
    \end{align*}
    the quadratic form $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$ is a completely Dirichlet form.

label: thm:char_bdd
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:char_bdd}
    A linear operator $L$ on $L^2(M)$ is the generator of a quantum Dirichlet form if and only if there exist
    \begin{itemize}
        \item an $M$-$M$ correspondence $\mathcal H$,
        \item an anti-unitary involution $\mathcal J\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$,
        \item a strongly continuous one-parameter group $(\mathcal V_s)_{s\in\mathbb R}$ on $\mathcal H$ with $\mathcal V_{-i/2}$ accretive,
        \item a bounded operator $\delta\colon L^2(M)\to\mathcal H$
    \end{itemize}
    satisfying
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item $\mathcal H=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{x\delta(a)y\mid a\in L^2(M),x,y\in M\}$,
        \item $\mathcal J(x\eta y)=y^\ast (\mathcal J\eta)x^\ast$, $\mathcal V_s(x\eta y)=\sigma^\varphi_s(x)(\mathcal V_s\eta)\sigma^\varphi_s(y)$ for all $x,y\in M$, $\eta\in\mathcal H$, $s\in\mathbb R$,
        \item $\mathcal V_s\mathcal J=\mathcal J \mathcal V_s$ for all $s\in\mathbb R$,
        \item $\delta\circ J=\mathcal J\circ\delta$, $\delta\circ \Delta_\varphi^{is}=\mathcal V_s\circ\delta$,
        \item $\delta(x\Omega_\varphi y)=x\delta(\Omega_\varphi y)+\delta(x\Omega_\varphi)y$ for all $x,y\in M$
    \end{enumerate}
    such that
    \begin{equation*}
        L=\delta^\ast\delta.
    \end{equation*}
    Moreover, if $(\mathcal H^\prime,\mathcal J^\prime,(\mathcal V_s^\prime)_{s\in\mathbb R},\delta^\prime)$ is a quadruple consisting of a self-dual correspondence $(\mathcal H^\prime,\mathcal J^\prime)$, a strongly continuous group $(\mathcal V^\prime_s)_{s\in\mathbb R}$ on $\mathcal H^\prime$ and a bounded operator $\delta^\prime\colon L^2(M)\to \mathcal H^\prime$ satisfying (i)--(v) above, then there exists a unique unitary bimodule map $\Theta\colon \mathcal H\to \mathcal H^\prime$ such that $\Theta\circ \mathcal J=\mathcal J^\prime\circ\Theta$, $\Theta\circ \mathcal V_s=\mathcal V_s^\prime\circ \Theta$ for all $s\in \mathbb R$ and $\Theta\circ \delta=\delta^\prime$.
    
    The operator $L$ commutes strongly with $\Delta_\varphi$ if and only if $\mathcal V_{-i/2}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator.

label: lem:res_mod_group_form
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:res_mod_group_form}
    If $\mathcal E$ is a conservative completely Dirichlet form, then $(\Delta_\varphi^{it})_{t\in\mathbb R}$ leaves $\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$ globally invariant and its restriction to $(\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E),\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal E})$ is a strongly continuous group.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: We have already seen in \Cref{lem:bound_mod_grp_form} that $\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$ is globally invariant under $(\Delta_\varphi^{it})_{t\in\mathbb R}$ and $\lVert\Delta_\varphi^{it}a\rVert_{\mathcal E}\leq e^{\pi\lvertt\rvert}\lVerta\rVert_{\mathcal E}$ for all $a\in\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$ and $t\in\mathbb R$. Let $L$ be the positive self-adjoint operator associated with $\mathcal E$. To show strong continuity, it is therefore \cite[Theorem I.5.8]{EN00} enough to prove that $t\mapsto \mathcal E(b,\Delta_\varphi^{it}a)$ is continuous at $t=0$ for all $b\in \operatorname{dom}(L)$. This follows immediately from $\mathcal E(b,\Delta_\varphi^{it}a)=\langle Lb,\Delta_\varphi^{it}a\rangle_2$ and the strong continuity of $(\Delta_\varphi^{it})$ with respect to the $L^2$-norm.

title: Definition
body_md: If $\mathcal E$ is a conservative completely Dirichlet form, let $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ be the subset of $L^2(M)$ consisting of all elements $x\Omega_\varphi$ for which $x\in M$ is analytic for $\sigma^\varphi$, $\sigma^\varphi_z(x)\Omega_\varphi\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$ for all $z\in\mathbb C$ and the map $z\mapsto \sigma^\varphi_z(x)\Omega_\varphi$ is entire analytic with respect to the form norm $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal E}$. We call $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ the \emph{Tomita algebra associated with $\mathcal E$}. Moreover, let $A_{\mathcal E}$ denote the norm closure of $\{x\in M\mid x\Omega_\varphi\in \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}\}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The name ``Tomita algebra associated with $\mathcal E$'' is justified by \Cref{cor:Tomita_subalgebra} below. Note that in the GNS-symmetric case, it suffices to require that $z\mapsto \sigma^\varphi_z(x)\Omega_\varphi$ is analytic for the $L^2$-norm by \cite[Lemma 6.6]{Wir22b}. Thus the definition of $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ from \cite[Definition 6.4]{Wir22b} coincides with the one given here in the GNS-symmetric case.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:analytic_gen_mod_grp_accretive}
    If $\mathcal E$ is a quantum Dirichlet form and $(V_s)_{s\in\mathbb R}$ denotes the restriction of $(\Delta_\varphi^{is})_{s\in\mathbb R}$ to $(\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E),\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal E})$, then $V_{-i/2}$ is accretive.

title: Proof

title: Remark
body_md:
The preceding theorem can also be checked directly without using \Cref{thm:char_bdd}. By the approximation argument given in the proof above, it suffices to consider bounded quantum Dirichlet forms. If $\mathcal E$ is bounded, then $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal E}$ and $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ are equivalent, hence $V_{-i/2}=\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}$ and $\Delta_\varphi^{1/4}\operatorname{dom}(\sigma^\varphi_{-i/2})\Omega_\varphi$ is a core for $V_{-i/2}$. Let $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be the quantum Markov semigroup associated with $\mathcal E$ and let $\mathcal L$ denote its generator. If $x\in \operatorname{dom}(\sigma^\varphi_{-i/2})$, then
    \begin{align*}
        \operatorname{Re}\mathcal E(\Delta_\varphi^{1/4}x\Omega_\varphi,\Delta_\varphi^{3/4}x\Omega_\varphi)
        &=\operatorname{Re}\langle \Delta_\varphi^{1/4}\mathcal L(x)\Omega_\varphi,\Delta_\varphi^{3/4}x\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\operatorname{Re}\langle \Delta_\varphi^{1/2}\mathcal L(x)\Omega_\varphi,\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}x\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\operatorname{Re}\langle x^\ast\Omega_\varphi,\mathcal L(x)^\ast\Omega_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\frac 1 2\varphi(x\mathcal L(x)^\ast+\mathcal L(x)x^\ast)\\
        &=\frac1  2\lim_{t\to 0}\frac 1 t\varphi(x x^\ast-\Phi_t(x)\Phi_t(x)^\ast)
    \end{align*}
    The last expression is positive by the Kadison--Schwarz inequality.

title: Lemma
body_md: If $\mathcal E$ is a quantum Dirichlet form, then $A_{\mathcal E}$ is a strong$^\ast$ dense unital $C^\ast$-subalgebra of $M$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: It follows from Corollary \ref{cor:Tomita_subalgebra} that $\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})$ is a unital $\ast$-subalgebra of $M$. Let $N=\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})^{\prime\prime}$. As a consequence of Lemma \ref{lem:res_mod_group_form}, the set $\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})$ and thus also $N$ is invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$. By Takesaki's theorem, there exists a unique $\varphi$-preserving conditional expectation $E\colon M\to N$, which has the property that $E(x)\Omega_\varphi$ is the orthogonal projection of $x\Omega_\varphi$ onto $\overline{N\Omega_\varphi}$ for $x\in M$. However, since $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ is a form core for $\mathcal E$, it is in particular dense in $L^2(M)$. Therefore $E=\mathrm{id}$ and $N=M$. The strong$^\ast$ density of $A_{\mathcal E}=\overline{\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})}^{\lVert\cdot\rVert}$ in $M$ is now a consequence of the Kaplansky density theorem.

title: Proposition
body_md: The operator $\mathcal V_{-i/2}$ is accretive.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have to show that $\operatorname{Re}\langle \xi,\mathcal V_{-i/2}\xi\rangle_{\mathcal H}\geq 0$ for all $\xi\in\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal V_{-i/2})$. By \Cref{lem:core_V_z}, we may assume that $\xi=\sum_{j=1}^m \pi_l(a_j)\cdot\delta(b_j)$ with $a_j,b_j\in\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ for $j\in \{1,\dots,m\}$. Moreover, \Cref{lem:anatytic_ext_V} that implies $\mathcal V_{-i/2}\xi=\sum_{j=1}^m \pi_l(\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}a_j)\delta(\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}b_j)$. If we combine this with the definition of $\delta$ and $\mathcal H$, we obtain
    \begin{align*}
        \operatorname{Re}\langle\xi,\mathcal V_{-i/2}\xi\rangle&=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{j,k=1}^m \langle \pi_l(a_j)\delta(b_j),\pi_l(\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}a_k)\delta(\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}b_k)\rangle_{\mathcal H}\\
        &=\lim_{n\to\omega}\operatorname{Re}\sum_{j,k=1}^m \langle \pi_l(a_j)\delta^{(n)}(b_j),\pi_l(\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}a_k)\delta^{(n)}(\Delta_\varphi^{1/2}b_k)\rangle_{\mathcal H^{(n)}}\\
        &=\lim_{n\to\omega}\operatorname{Re}\left\langle\sum_{j=1}^m \pi_l(a_j)\delta^{(n)}(b_j),\mathcal V^{(n)}_{-i/2}\left(\sum_{j=1}^m \pi_l(a_j)\cdot \delta^{(n)}(b_j)\right)\right\rangle_{\mathcal H^{(n)}}.
    \end{align*}
    This last expression is non-negative by our result in the bounded case.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{prop:deform_unitary_group}, we get a Tomita correspondence $(\mathcal H,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_s))$, a strongly continuous group $(\mathcal V_s)$ on $\mathcal H$ and a bounded derivation $\delta\colon L^2(M)\to \mathcal H$ such that $\delta\circ J_\varphi=\mathcal J\circ \delta$, $\delta\circ \Delta_\varphi^{is}=\mathcal V_s\circ \delta$ and $\mathcal E(a)=\lVert\delta(a)\rVert_2^2$. Moreover, if $A$ denotes the generator of $\mathcal V_s$, then there exists a bounded self-adjoint bimodule map $B\colon \mathcal H\to \mathcal H$ such that $A+B$ is the generator of $(\mathcal U_s)$.

    Following \cite[Section 4.2]{Wir22b}, we can define the operator-valued free Araki--Woods algebra $\hat M=\Gamma_0(\mathcal H,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_s))$ over $(\mathcal H,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_s)_{s\in \mathbb R})$, which comes with a canonical faithful normal conditional expectation $E\colon \hat M\to M$ and a canonical identification $L^2(\hat M)\cong \mathcal F(_M\mathcal H_M)\supset \mathcal H$ \cite[Theorem 4.15]{Wir22b}. Moreover, $\Delta_{\varphi\circ E}^{is}|_\mathcal H=\mathcal U_s$ by \cite[Theorem 5.18]{KW25}.

    Since $B\colon\mathcal H\to \mathcal H$ is a bounded self-adjoint bimodule map, we can extend it to a bounded self-adjoint bimodule map on $\mathcal F(_M\mathcal H_M)$ by defining $B|_{L^2(M)}=\mathrm{id}_{L^2(M)}$ and $B|_{\mathcal H^{\otimes_\varphi n}}=\lVertB\rVert(B/\lVertB\rVert)^{\otimes_\varphi n}$. Since both $B$ and $\Delta_\varphi$ leave $\mathcal H$ invariant, it follows that the group generated by $i\log\Delta_{\varphi\circ E}-B$ leaves $\mathcal H$ invariant, and since its generator is an extension of the generator of $(\mathcal V_s)_{s\in\mathbb R}$, it is easy to see that $\mathcal V_s$ is a restriction of $e^{s(i\log\Delta_{\varphi\circ E}+B)}$
